Before you say "but it's just Pokemon with guns", take a moment to read this review. 

Palworld initially started out as essentially a creature catching game with guns and some questionable pal designs, but has come a long way, even before it's 1.0 release. At first glance, it seems like it might be a little lackluster, with a limited character creation set, next to no dialogue, and NPC's that survive about as long as the usual helldiver in combat scenarios they obviously were not designed to get involved in. 

But what the game doesn't lack? An expansive world, explosions, base building, QUESTIONABLE pal designs (in a sort of suggestive way, not the potential rip-off kind), and lots and lots of guns! You start out, a simple beach bob, not unlike Ark Survival. Mildly chilled, you wander inland and start to gather food, build shelter, and look at the spires in the distance before night falls. As time passes, you then learn you can put the massive unemployment of the Palpagos Islands to good use, be it psychotic squirrels in a factory, using a fox as a flamethrower, and having Cindera- I mean Verdash to tend to the fields. As time goes on even further, you'll take on ancient entities, legendary pals, and perhaps even challenge Senator Armstrong (if you chose to mod your game as such).

Overall, would recommend this game.

If you liked Pokemon, especially Legends Arceus, you will love this. Only dissapointing thing is the base building styles and building blocks variations.

This is a game that has perfectly combined mechanics across several different games to create something more than the sum of its parts. And the developers did it with one of the biggest, most litigious game companies on EARTH breathing down their necks for like 2 years, for completely nonsensical patents.

Honestly, the panthalus boss fight alone is worth half the price of the game. The craziest, most cinematic boss fight I've ever done that had me wishing I could fight him for the first time again. The other half comes from using that panthalus to fly around the map and give enemy bases a free all expenses paid (non-consensual) trip to the Mariana trench.

Besides that, I love how the player is encouraged to fight alongside the pals instead of just giving them orders. You can obviously ride them around in battle to use their attacks manually. But there are also pals that boost your attack, change the elemental type of your weapon so you AND your pal can hit the target for super effective damage, and some pals that BECOME your weapon. Compared to pokemon who gives you 6 mon slots, you only have 5 party pal slots because YOU are the 6th fighter. Outside of combat, the way the pals help you at the base makes them feel so alive, and it makes your base feel lived in. It makes you feel that you are living and working alongside your pals. There are plenty of memes about mistreating pals, and that is an option, but I always give mine the best available beds and food, and build my bases in scenic locations (the human NPCs on the other hand never see the light of day in their human powered generators). I even have a tradition to build a 'Valhalla' base for my early game party pals who were with me from the very start but got replaced as I progressed.

My criticisms? Please nerf torrential blast; the way it comes out instantly and moves DIAGONALly afterwards makes it impossible to dodge. I'm also on the FENCE on the story; it's not really worth following. Also, please make it so that pals use their moves in the order I've assigned them. That would make aggregate combos so much smoother.

Overall, incredible game. Easily my 2nd favorite game, only behind stardew valley, but there is zero shame in coming 2nd to stardew valley.

Honestly, this game captures exactly what I love about ARK's survival and base-building loop, but mixes it with the monster-taming experience I’ve been wanting from Pokémon for years. The core gameplay of exploring, building up a base, and managing your pals is incredibly addictive. It’s super satisfying to just chill and build out your production lines.

That being said, there are some minor quality of life issues that keep it from being perfect, mainly with the game's pacing. The tech tree is really dense, and it’s way too easy to outpace your technology just by leveling up naturally. I constantly find myself 20 or more levels ahead of the gear I can actually craft, which feels a bit weird. I'll be unlocking crazy Ancient Technology in my menu, but back at my base, I'm still trying to figure out how to mass-produce mid-tier Plasteel.

The base crafting system also feels a bit too basic for how complicated the late-game recipes get. It desperately needs some standard survival QoL updates. It would be huge if we could queue up multiple different items at the same bench, or if the game would just auto-craft prerequisite components if you already have the raw materials sitting in your base chests. Having a few dedicated storage slots on the crafting benches themselves specifically for those materials would also save so much tedious inventory management.

Even with the weird leveling curve and the clunky crafting menus, the foundation is really solid. If the devs can polish up the crafting logistics and balance the leveling a bit, it's easily one of the best survival games out there right now. Definitely worth picking up.

Palworld is easily one of the greatest games Ive ever played, at least for the first 70 hours, more specifically, I mean the journey, and all of its subcontents included, to the final boss of the game, the first true blind journey that is possible. Not knowing whats coming next, experiencing all the really well designed creatures that roam the various landscapes, fighting said creatures and even capturing them, raiding preconstructed bases, discovering what pals do and having a good time with them, and simply just exploring in however way you so please, its great stuff, truly a breath of fresh air from the mass amounts of mindless "modern gamer pleasing media" garbage that pollutes games from the common age nowadays. I would say Ive never really played a game before that truly MAKES you experience all of, or at least most of, the content it has to offer, all the tools they provide to you, skills and tricks as well, upgrading things, giving the right modifiers to your pals, organizing your base into a factory.. you can turn the early game slowness into a full on production simulator and its very satisfying to get to that point, I love the quests the pal labor research lab sends you on and how rewarding they end up being in the end as well. I suppose some things can be painfully slow to craft at times, but if this is an issue you are facing, you can most likely make it not an issue with the right modifier, the surgery table is what I refer to, there too is work speed for each pal hidden in the soul distributor statue. Palworld does a lot of stuff right, and I would highly suggest you go and witness this for yourself, I dont wish to spoil things this early into the review. But it doesnt do everything right, and this is precisely why I withheld my review for this game until I experienced ALL of its content, ALL of it, as I loved the first 70ish hours of my very first playthrough of this game, I never looked up guides, I never knew anything about it beforehand apart from some stupid crap revolving around Nintendo trying to sue it because of pokeballs or whatever. But lets start off simple! I feel this game needed some kind of level scaling, its a shame to see the Terraria crossover stuff be completely worthless after level 40 is well past your point of existence, and its also a shame to accidentally over-level for a zone you didnt even know existed yet. now that areas a joke and probably not even worth your time anymore. It is good, however, that rewards for slaying the open world bosses are just perma stat enhancers as well as high amount of their loot table material drops, this fixes the issue many games have that give you some trinket you never end up using. For the most part I actually would say the main game progression is well handled, in terms of level scaling and loot placements, but side content is just simply poorly handled. Dungeons are a neat idea, but the time restraints regarding access into them are annoying to deal with, and you see a lot of the same designs that never play differently from eachother other than potentially different pal types being inside them. The Arena is heeping seeping ass water, the achievements tied to the unnecessarily large amount of effigies are absolutely bonkers crazy, and the sheer bullasstomshittery that is the design behind the hardmode versions of the tower bosses, are horrible! Listen to me when I say that it is NOT fun, or good game design, to be FORCED (if you wish for the achievement, at least) to float around sections of the map which could be as large as a real life city, looking for little glowing balls. Bonus terrible points for areas of the map that hide the stupid little shits underneath crap, forcing you to actually go to the ground and use your eyeballs rather than use the poor rendering distance to your advantage to see the effigy glows from afar way up in the sky with a good flying pal. Best advice to fix it? Remove every single effigy from the game, and replace them with just a stat bonus hidden behind an actual challenge you need to overcome that requires skill, like secret dungeons or something unique to each area that the effigies are placed in now. It would be FUN to go and find a secret dungeon hidden somewhere in the world, even more so if the game hints at their existence through the usage of NPCS or such, it is not fun to go and waste your life staring at the ground from miles up in the sky for over 300 goddamn glowing balls haphazardly placed in corners and crannies wherever the hell the designers felt like at the time. Next, the arena. Its design is a joke, the achievements tied to it do not require skill, rewards you can get from it are so easily obtained from other sources and take way too long to actually obtain thanks to the abysmal drop rates of the arena currency, they require you to put aside 30 hours of your life just to experience the same stupid battles over, and over, and over, and over again. Hold your fire, do NOT, EVER, attempt the legendary arena tier challenges. Dont! Im giving you advice, they are not worth your time, sanity, and especially not worth the effort. I'll tell you what are not optional however if you wish to 100% this game, and thats the hardmode towers. The completion rate, at the time of this review, for the champion of palpagos island achievement, is 3.1 percent. This is for a reason, as the difficulty spike from ANYTHING else in the entire game, including the final boss itself which was a tremendously well designed encounter by the way, is out of this entire galaxy. For example, lets say in a game you go from being tasked with fighting slimes, to fighting Cthulu a few moments later with the same gear and equipment. Each tower, on hardmode, is such a ridiculously punishing, barely rewarding ordeal that requires you to use every single trick in the entire book just to overcome. I would be here for hours typing all my smaller complaints for these towers, but I'll simplify it with the main problem, and that is you need to grind way, way, WAY too much just to have the correct lineups for each battle, all just for an achievement. Seriously, the first pal tower on hardmode is more difficult than the final boss of the game? Thank the great and mighty Gabriel Ultrakill that you dont need to do ALL the towers at least.. I suppose the best thing to say for each tower is you need to fight them in different ways, and equip the gear you actually need, no gear slots can be wasted for these brutal encounters. Ammo spent during the fights? Gotta go recraft it if you lost, or if you won. Pal die during that battle? Congrats, go wait ten minutes before you can try again, or waste a revive potion if youre lazy. You get cosmetics for actually triumphing these fights. Just cosmetics. Are the hardmode towers inoffensive? Are they fun? I honestly dont know. There was a lot of endless murder in the world tree and lots of ancient relic recycling to get my hands on new stat modifiers required for these awful battles, which is genuinely what it feels like your success chances come down to sometimes. When I saw that six of these hard tower versions were required for the achievement, two weeks ago? I really thought I didnt have it in me to slog through it all. It took way too long of my life just to have the pals (and myself for Gabriel's sake) in my lineups even barely strong enough just to not get instakilled by any attack these bosses tossed at me, and strong enough to out-damage the time limits. I still dont feel accomplished for these towers, I feel relieved it is over so I can do literally anything else in life that are not those towers ever again. In the end, I fully believe one should experience Palworld.. but maybe they should jump ship when they have seen its fantastic ending, and after you've had a lovely time with the pals that suit you best on the amazing journey that leads up to that point.
